name: Southern Lacandon / lacandón del sur
confidence_why: Two first-hand descriptions disagree and the disagreement is unresolved: Mojica Hernández & Martínez Corripio 2018, checked against the source, describe weight-sensitive stress that is final by default, while Baer & Baer 2018 place the accent on the first syllable of the root (see the dissent); 2 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

catalog_quote: El lacandón del norte presenta un patrón acentual trocaico (*.), en el cual el acento recae en la primera sílaba de una palabra bisilábica. ... El lacandón del sur y el yucateco presentan el mismo tipo de patrón acentual yámbico (.*), el cual se caracteriza porque el acento de una palabra bisilábica recae en la segunda sílaba ... En ambas lenguas la sílaba con mayor prominencia acentual es la sílaba final. Cabe mencionar que tanto en lacandón del norte, como en lacandón del sur y en yucateco las sílabas que se encuentran a final de palabra siempre son cerradas (CVC). (4) Acento final en lacandón del sur a. [pe.ˈpen] ‘mariposa b. [ku.ˈʃup] ‘epazote’ c. [pet.ˈhɐʔ] ‘laguna’ ... el lacandón del sur y el yucateco presentan vocales largas. En este sentido, ambas lenguas son sensibles al peso silábico (Mojica Hernández, 2012). De tal manera que cuando aparece una vocal larga como núcleo de una sílaba no-final, el acento es atraído hacia la sílaba que contiene vocal larga o re-articulada, como se muestra en los ejemplos (6) y (7). En el caso del lacandón del sur, se observa que las sílabas con vocal larga, ejemplos (6a) y (6b), o rearticulada (6c), llevan el acento de palabra. ... (6) Acento en lacandón del sur a. [ˈk’ɐ:m.buɾ] ‘faisán’ b. [ˈmi:.sip] ‘escoba’ c. [ˈʧɐˀɐ.nɘɾ] ‘elote’ ... En cuanto al lacandón del norte, si bien no presenta vocales largas, el acento fijo siempre aparece en la primera sílaba de una palabra bisilábica.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: Two systems under one glottocode. Southern Lacandon (Lacanjá Chansayab): stress on the final syllable by default; a non-final syllable with a long or rearticulated (laryngealized) vowel is heavy and takes the stress instead (e.g. [ˈmi.sip] 'broom', [ˈk’ɐ:m.buɾ] 'pheasant' vs [pe.ˈpen] 'butterfly', [to.ˈɾok] 'iguana'). Northern Lacandon (Nahá, Metzabok): no contrastive/phonetic vowel length in the young speakers studied and fixed stress on the first syllable of bisyllabic words ([ˈpe.pen], [ˈmi.sip], [ˈto.ɾok]). The reading 'weight-sensitive' is assigned for Southern Lacandon; Northern Lacandon would be 'fixed: initial syllable'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed in Mojica 2014. Bennett 2016 (p. 500) points to Herrera Zendejas 2014 Ch.10 for 'possible phonetic evidence of secondary stress in Lacandon' (not seen first-hand).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; data are bisyllabic (max. three-syllable) words elicited in isolation from word lists (2 LN speakers from Nahá, 2 LS speakers from Lacanjá Chansayab, ages 21-30). Author notes that LN word-final syllables are always closed (CVC) and that LN's apparent loss of vowel length may be a change in progress, so the LN fixed pattern is tentative (p. 59: 'puede implicar que esta lengua presente un patrón de acento fijo'). Southern Lacandon is also reported (Wikipedia citing Mojica & Martínez Corripio 2018; Bennett 2016 citing Canger 1995 ms.) to have high/low lexical tone on long vowels, which the thesis does not analyse.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, citation forms elicited in isolation ('palabras producidas de manera aislada'); acoustic (duration/formant) study, stress judged perceptually plus duration; no phrase-level statement.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog laca1243 'Lacandon' has no dialect children, but the source (Mojica Hernández 2014) treats Northern Lacandon (LN: Nahá and Metzabok, Ocosingo, Chiapas; ~200-250 speakers) and Southern Lacandon (LS: Lacanjá Chansayab; ~300-500 speakers) as separate languages with different stress systems: LN fixed initial (trochaic, bisyllables), LS final/weight-sensitive (iambic, like Yucatec). The 'weight-sensitive' reading is for Southern Lacandon, the variety also described by Hofling 2014 and Martínez Corripio 2018; Bruce 1968 and Bergqvist 2008 describe Northern Lacandon speakers. No separate glottocodes exist for the two varieties.

Cabe mencionar que tanto en lacandón del norte, como en lacandón del sur y en yucateco las sílabas que se encuentran a final de palabra siempre son cerradas (CVC). [...] ambas lenguas son sensibles al peso silábico (Mojica Hernández, 2012). De tal manera que cuando aparece una vocal larga como núcleo de una sílaba no-final, el acento es atraído hacia la sílaba que contiene vocal larga o re-articulada [...] las sílabas con vocal larga, ejemplos (6a) y (6b), o rearticulada (6c), llevan el acento de palabra.
new_statements.translation: Southern Lacandon and Yucatec show the same type of iambic stress pattern (.*), characterized by the stress of a disyllabic word falling on the second syllable [...] In both languages the syllable with the greatest stress prominence is the final syllable. It should be noted that in Northern Lacandon, Southern Lacandon and Yucatec alike, word-final syllables are always closed (CVC). [...] both languages are sensitive to syllable weight (Mojica Hernández 2012). Thus, when a long vowel appears as the nucleus of a non-final syllable, stress is attracted to the syllable containing the long or rearticulated vowel [...] syllables with a long vowel, examples (6a) and (6b), or a rearticulated vowel (6c), carry the word stress.

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement and same weight mechanism as the existing statement from the first author's 2014 UAM thesis (final stress in disyllables, attracted to a non-final syllable with a long or rearticulated vowel), now with acoustic data and journal pagination. The catalog record for laca1243 has an empty rule field; this article supplies the rule. The Northern Lacandon statements in the same article (trochaic, fixed initial stress, §5.3.1 p. 88 and p. 91) concern a different variety (Nahá/Metzabok), not the catalog's Southern Lacandon.
new_statements.rule_in_words: In Southern Lacandon (Lacanjá Chansayab) word stress is final by default in disyllables (final syllables are always closed CVC): [pe.ˈpen] 'butterfly', [ku.ˈʃup] 'epazote', [pet.ˈhɐʔ] 'lagoon', [to.ˈɾok] 'iguana'. A non-final syllable whose nucleus is a long vowel or a rearticulated (glottalized VʔV) vowel attracts the stress instead: [ˈk’ɐ:m.buɾ] 'pheasant', [ˈmi.sip] 'broom', [ˈʧɐˀɐ.nɘɾ] 'ear of corn'. The conclusions (p. 99) restate that in Southern Lacandon and Yucatec phonetic vowel length 'defines the position of word stress, since both languages are sensitive to syllable weight', whereas Northern Lacandon has fixed stress on the first syllable of a disyllable.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. The authors add (p. 93) that a proper syllabic analysis is still needed 'para determinar los tipos de acento' shown for the three languages, i.e. the stress typing is offered as provisional. Only disyllables are exemplified.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog laca1243 'Lacandon' (ISO lac) has dialect children Lacanjá (laca1244) and Najá; the catalog item is labelled Southern Lacandon. The 2018 article's Southern Lacandon data come from Lacanjá Chansayab, Chiapas (Table on p. 51: ~500 speakers), and its Northern Lacandon data from Nahá/Metzabok. The article warns (fn. 3, p. 52) that Northern Lacandon speakers living in Lacanjá Chansayab show contact features. Bruce 1968 is a grammar of the Najá (Northern) variety.

tone_statements.citation: Sobrino Gómez, Martín. 2022. Análisis acústico y descripción de procesos fonológicos del maya lacandón (Lacanjá). Lingüística Mexicana. Nueva Época 4(2): 153-178.
tone_statements.quote: Hofling (2014: 28) explica que el sistema vocálico de la variedad de Lacanjá únicamente presenta tonos en el habla de los adultos mayores, en tanto que en los hablantes jóvenes se perdió la distinción. En los datos obtenidos de los participantes (quienes no están en el rango de edad para ser adultos mayores) no se encuentra evidencia sobre un contraste tonal. ... Como puede apreciarse, en ambas palabras la tonía de la vocal se mantiene estable, y tales trayectorias no reflejan un contraste tonal. ... Confirmamos que en el habla de los participantes de la investigación (hablantes jóvenes) no se encuentra distinción o contraste tonal en las vocales largas.
tone_statements.translation: Hofling (2014: 28) explains that the vowel system of the Lacanjá variety has tones only in the speech of older adults, whereas among young speakers the distinction was lost. In the data obtained from the participants (who are not in the age range of older adults) no evidence of a tonal contrast is found. ... As can be seen, in both words the pitch of the vowel stays stable, and these trajectories do not reflect a tonal contrast. ... We confirm that in the speech of the study participants (young speakers) no tonal distinction or contrast is found on long vowels.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 163-164 (vowel section, figs. 5-6) and Conclusiones p. 174; see also pp. 175-176
tone_statements.summary: No tonal contrast in the long vowels of younger Lacanjá (Southern Lacandon) speakers; a high vs low tone contrast on long vowels (as in Yucatec) is reported only for older adults, second-hand from Hofling 2014: 28; contrasts carried instead by vowel length and modal vs laryngealized phonation; the northern variety is said to have lost tone earlier. No statement on stress or on a tone-bearing unit…

tone_statements.citation: Hofling, Charles Andrew. 2018. Cambio diacrónico en la familia lingüística yucatecana. Cuadernos de Lingüística de El Colegio de México 5(1): 6-46.
tone_statements.quote: Así, las palabras del proto-yucatecano con la forma CVHC, donde H representa una fricativa velar o glotal, resultaron tener la forma CV́VC en yucateco y entre hablantes mayores de lacandón del sur de Lacanjá. En este último sitio, los hablantes más jóvenes perdieron la distinción entre tono alto y tono bajo y solo tienen vocales largas (Hofling 2014: 28). El lacandón del norte no tiene una distinción de tono y muestra variaciones entre vocales largas y cortas ... Por un lado, el yucateco y el lacandón del sur tienen tono y longitud vocálica, en contraste con el lacandón del norte, itzaj, y mopán.
tone_statements.translation: Thus proto-Yucatecan words of the shape CVHC, where H is a velar or glottal fricative, came to have the shape CV́VC in Yucatec and among older speakers of Southern Lacandon at Lacanjá. There, the younger speakers lost the distinction between high tone and low tone and have only long vowels (Hofling 2014: 28). Northern Lacandon has no tone distinction and shows variation between long and short vowels ... On the one hand, Yucatec and Southern Lacandon have tone and vowel length, in contrast with Northern Lacandon, Itzaj and Mopan.
tone_statements.locator: §2 'Fonología' (discussion of Cuadro 1; also Cuadros 17 and 25 in §3) and §4 'Conclusión' (Cuadro 32); pp. 6-46, summary statement at p. 38 per Sobrino 2022
tone_statements.summary: Southern Lacandon (older Lacanjá speakers): two-way lexical tone on long vowels, high (CV́VC < *CVhC) vs low, as in Yucatec; younger speakers: length only, no tone; Northern Lacandon: no tone, unstable length. Grammatical tone in Southern Lacandon: possessed-noun class with long low-tone vowel; mediopassive marked by long high-tone vowel. No downstep/stress information.

tone_statements.citation: Sobrino Gómez, Carlos Martín. 2018. El sistema fonológico protoyucatecano: reconstrucción y desarrollo. Tesis de Doctorado en Lingüística, Centro de Estudios Lingüísticos y Literarios, El Colegio de México. 286 pp. (dir. Julia Pozas Loyo).
tone_statements.quote: Hofling (2014, 2015) sugiere que el sistema vocálico de la variedad de Lacanjá tiene tonos. No obstante, en los datos actuales no encuentro evidencia sobre un contraste tonal, sea este léxico o morfológico. En la Figura 3.18 se muestra, en maya yucateco, el contraste tonal léxico de las palabras kàaʃ ‘gallina’ y k’áaʃ ‘monte’. ... Las formas cognadas en lacandón del sur se muestran en la Figura 19. Como puede apreciarse, en ambas palabras la tonía de la vocal manifiesta un ascenso y tales trayectorias no reflejan un contraste tonal. ... al separarse del yucateco, el lacandón dejó de considerar la frecuencia fundamental como significativa, pero sin perder la longitud vocálica en las palabras.
tone_statements.translation: Hofling (2014, 2015) suggests that the vowel system of the Lacanjá variety has tones. However, in the present data I find no evidence of a tonal contrast, whether lexical or morphological. Figure 3.18 shows, in Yucatec Maya, the lexical tonal contrast of the words kàaʃ 'hen' and k'áaʃ 'bush'. ... The cognate forms in Southern Lacandon are shown in Figure 19. As can be seen, in both words the pitch of the vowel shows a rise and such trajectories do not reflect a tonal contrast. ... on separating from Yucatec, Lacandon stopped treating fundamental frequency as significant, but without losing vowel length in words.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 121-122, Cap. 3 §3.3 Vocales (before Figs. 3.18-3.19); last sentence p. 261, §6.9
tone_statements.summary: Author finds no lexical or grammatical tonal contrast in Southern (Lacanjá) Lacandon, contra Hofling; F0 of kaaʃ and k'aaʃ both rise. Yucatec toned long vowels match plain long vowels in Lacandon.

tone_statements.citation: Cook, Suzanne (Lacandon Cultural Heritage Project, University of Victoria). n.d. [online since 2004]. Phonology and Phonetics (sections 'Stress' and 'Tone'). Web page of the Lacandon Cultural Heritage / DOBES Lacandon documentation project, web.uvic.ca/lacandon/phon.htm.
tone_statements.quote: Primary stress may fall on either the ultimate or penultimate syllable of a root. The alternation appears to be stylistic rather than phonemic, e.g., [péta7] 'lake', [7uDún] 'turkey', [tóDok] 'lizard', [äkná7] 'moon', [áak'a7] 'night'. ... However, it appears that tone does occur in some Lacandón dialects. A southern dialect spoken in San Quintin has tone (Canger 1970); another southern dialect spoken in Lacanhá may not--but could (Hofling, 2000, personal communication). Tone does not seem to be contrastive in the northern dialect spoken in Naha. Its presence serves stylistic rather than grammatical ends (Bruce 1968).
tone_statements.locator: web page 'Phonology and Phonetics', section headings 'Stress' and 'Tone' (end of page, before 'Go to: Morphology and Syntax')
tone_statements.summary: Northern Lacandon (Naha): no contrastive tone, pitch variation stylistic; word stress on final or penultimate syllable of the root in free (stylistic) variation, i.e. no fixed contrastive stress position stated. Southern dialects: San Quintín reported tonal (Canger 1970), Lacanjá uncertain (as of 2000).

sources.note: 'Tone' section: following Fisher (1973) and Fox (1978), Lacandon lacks the pitch contours of Yucatec proper; tone reported for the southern San Quintín dialect (Canger 1970), uncertain for Lacanjá (Hofling p.c. 2000); not contrastive in the northern Naha dialect, where pitch serves stylistic ends (Bruce 1968). 'Stress' section: primary stress on the ultimate or penultimate syllable of a root, the alternation stylistic rather than phonemic; compounds stress the second root or both.

tone.quote: Primary stress may fall on either the ultimate or penultimate syllable of a root. The alternation appears to be stylistic rather than phonemic, e.g., [péta7] 'lake', [7uDún] 'turkey', [tóDok] 'lizard', [äkná7] 'moon', [áak'a7] 'night'. ... However, it appears that tone does occur in some Lacandón dialects. A southern dialect spoken in San Quintin has tone (Canger 1970); another southern dialect spoken in Lacanhá may not--but could (Hofling, 2000, personal communication). Tone does not seem to be contrastive in the northern dialect spoken in Naha. Its presence serves stylistic rather than grammatical ends (Bruce 1968).
tone.locator: web page 'Phonology and Phonetics', section headings 'Stress' and 'Tone' (end of page, before 'Go to: Morphology and Syntax')
tone.summary: Northern Lacandon (Naha): no contrastive tone, pitch variation stylistic; word stress on final or penultimate syllable of the root in free (stylistic) variation, i.e. no fixed contrastive stress position stated. Southern dialects: San Quintín reported tonal (Canger 1970), Lacanjá uncertain (as of 2000).
tone.says: 'Tone' section: following Fisher (1973) and Fox (1978), Lacandon lacks the pitch contours of Yucatec proper; tone reported for the southern San Quintín dialect (Canger 1970), uncertain for Lacanjá (Hofling p.c. 2000); not contrastive in the northern Naha dialect, where pitch serves stylistic ends (Bruce 1968). 'Stress' section: primary stress on the ultimate or penultimate syllable of a root, the alternation stylistic rather than phonemic; compounds stress the second root or both.

tone.translation: Hofling (2014: 28) explains that the vowel system of the Lacanjá variety has tones only in the speech of older adults, whereas among young speakers the distinction was lost. In the data obtained from the participants (who are not in the age range of older adults) no evidence of a tonal contrast is found. ... As can be seen, in both words the pitch of the vowel stays stable, and these trajectories do not reflect a tonal contrast. ... We confirm that in the speech of the study participants (young speakers) no tonal distinction or contrast is found on long vowels.
tone.summary: No tonal contrast in the long vowels of younger Lacanjá (Southern Lacandon) speakers; a high vs low tone contrast on long vowels (as in Yucatec) is reported only for older adults, second-hand from Hofling 2014: 28; contrasts carried instead by vowel length and modal vs laryngealized phonation; the northern variety is said to have lost tone earlier. No statement on stress or on a tone-bearing unit…

sources.quote: Así, las palabras del proto-yucatecano con la forma CVHC, donde H representa una fricativa velar o glotal, resultaron tener la forma CV́VC en yucateco y entre hablantes mayores de lacandón del sur de Lacanjá. En este último sitio, los hablantes más jóvenes perdieron la distinción entre tono alto y tono bajo y solo tienen vocales largas (Hofling 2014: 28). El lacandón del norte no tiene una distinción de tono y muestra variaciones entre vocales largas y cortas ... Por un lado, el yucateco y el lacandón del sur tienen tono y longitud vocálica, en contraste con el lacandón del norte, itzaj, y mopán.
sources.locator: §2 'Fonología' (discussion of Cuadro 1; also Cuadros 17 and 25 in §3) and §4 'Conclusión' (Cuadro 32); pp. 6-46, summary statement at p. 38 per Sobrino 2022
sources.note: Proto-Yucatecan *CVhC > CV́VC (high tone) in Yucatec and among older Southern Lacandon speakers of Lacanjá; younger Lacanjá speakers lost the high/low tone distinction and keep only long vowels (Hofling 2014: 28); Northern Lacandon has no tone distinction; grammatical tone shared by Yucatec and Southern Lacandon: a noun class takes a long low-tone vowel when possessed (Cuadro 17) and the mediopassive is marked by a long high-tone vowel (Cuadro 25); conclusion: Yucatec and Southern Lacandon have tone and vowel length, unlike Northern Lacandon, Itzaj and Mopan. Nothing on stress.

tone.translation: Thus proto-Yucatecan words of the shape CVHC, where H is a velar or glottal fricative, came to have the shape CV́VC in Yucatec and among older speakers of Southern Lacandon at Lacanjá. There, the younger speakers lost the distinction between high tone and low tone and have only long vowels (Hofling 2014: 28). Northern Lacandon has no tone distinction and shows variation between long and short vowels ... On the one hand, Yucatec and Southern Lacandon have tone and vowel length, in contrast with Northern Lacandon, Itzaj and Mopan.
tone.summary: Southern Lacandon (older Lacanjá speakers): two-way lexical tone on long vowels, high (CV́VC < *CVhC) vs low, as in Yucatec; younger speakers: length only, no tone; Northern Lacandon: no tone, unstable length. Grammatical tone in Southern Lacandon: possessed-noun class with long low-tone vowel; mediopassive marked by long high-tone vowel. No downstep/stress information.

sources.quote: Hofling (2014, 2015) sugiere que el sistema vocálico de la variedad de Lacanjá tiene tonos. No obstante, en los datos actuales no encuentro evidencia sobre un contraste tonal, sea este léxico o morfológico. En la Figura 3.18 se muestra, en maya yucateco, el contraste tonal léxico de las palabras kàaʃ ‘gallina’ y k’áaʃ ‘monte’. ... Las formas cognadas en lacandón del sur se muestran en la Figura 19. Como puede apreciarse, en ambas palabras la tonía de la vocal manifiesta un ascenso y tales trayectorias no reflejan un contraste tonal. ... al separarse del yucateco, el lacandón dejó de considerar la frecuencia fundamental como significativa, pero sin perder la longitud vocálica en las palabras.

tone.translation: Hofling (2014, 2015) suggests that the vowel system of the Lacanjá variety has tones. However, in the present data I find no evidence of a tonal contrast, whether lexical or morphological. Figure 3.18 shows, in Yucatec Maya, the lexical tonal contrast of the words kàaʃ 'hen' and k'áaʃ 'bush'. ... The cognate forms in Southern Lacandon are shown in Figure 19. As can be seen, in both words the pitch of the vowel shows a rise and such trajectories do not reflect a tonal contrast. ... on separating from Yucatec, Lacandon stopped treating fundamental frequency as significant, but without losing vowel length in words.
tone.summary: Author finds no lexical or grammatical tonal contrast in Southern (Lacanjá) Lacandon, contra Hofling; F0 of kaaʃ and k'aaʃ both rise. Yucatec toned long vowels match plain long vowels in Lacandon.
